name: EvilTokens
akas: UnSub (no named group / Storm-#### designation given in this post)
brief: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit disrupted EvilTokens, an AI chatbot platform sold via Telegram ($1,500 initiation + $500/month) that used AI "at every step of the attack chain" — analyzing compromised inboxes to identify trusted relationships, payment authorizations, and an organization's "money movers"; recommending fraud strategies and targets; and drafting impersonation messages. Investigators found evidence large portions of EvilTokens itself were "vibe coded," drawing on capabilities from multiple AI models. Initial access relied on device-code-style phishing that tricked victims into completing legitimate Microsoft sign-in flows. Within months of a February 2026 launch, the platform was linked to 12,000+ compromised inboxes across 10,000+ organizations worldwide (highest concentrations: US, Canada, UK, Australia, India, France), spanning wholesale distribution, construction, financial services, real estate, higher education, and healthcare. Court-authorized disruption (US District Court, Eastern District of Virginia) with partners Cloudflare, Coinbase, OpenAI, Railway, SpyCloud, Shadowserver, and TRM Labs, co-plaintiff Health-ISAC; UK authorities arrested two men (32, 38) on 2026-09-11. Microsoft's 40th court-authorized DCU disruption and its first against an "end-to-end AI-enabled cybercrime service." Microsoft
activity: Feb 2026 – Sep 2026 (launched Feb 2026; disruption action Sep 2026)
